findings.evidence: The account-deletion URL declared in both places — app.json:189 "accountDeletionUrl": "https://www.mama-et-bebe.com/delete-account.html" and store/listing.json:26 — returns HTTP 404 live (curl -L on 2026-09-30: delete-account.html -> 404, delete-account-en.html -> 404; privacy.html/support.html/index.html -> 200). The page exists only in the repo (website/delete-account.html, commit 9cae9fe) and was never deployed. Play Console's Data safety form requires a working web link where users can request deletion (outside the app), and Play checks it when it reviews the form. A 404 blocks the Data safety form or gets the app rejected.
findings.fix_hint: Deploy website/ (vercel deploy --prod from ../website, per website/README.md), then re-check both delete-account.html and delete-account-en.html return 200 before filling Play > App content > Data safety. First fix the wrong navigation path in that page (see F-004), or the page you deploy will be inaccurate.

findings.evidence: The emergency call button can dial another country's number. (1) OnboardingScreen.tsx:113 `const [country, setCountry] = useState('tunisia');` — region auto-detection (lines 133-147) maps only TN/FR/BE/MA/DZ, so every other device region (US, UK, CA, EG, SA, LB, ...) stays pre-selected as 'tunisia'. (2) The picker (OnboardingScreen.tsx:556-561, ProfileScreen.tsx:262-267) offers only tunisia/france/belgium/morocco/algeria/other. US/UK/CA are in EMERGENCY_NUMBERS (clinicalChecks.ts:253-258) but cannot be selected. (3) For country 'other', getEmergencyNumber returns null and resolveEmergencyNumber falls back to the UI language (clinicalChecks.ts:290-294: ar/tn -> '190', fr -> '15'). An Arabic-speaking user in Egypt or Saudi Arabia is shown '📞 … (190)', which is Tunisian SAMU, and a French speaker in Canada, Lebanon or Senegal gets '15'. This contradicts the code's own promise at clinicalChecks.ts:231 'never guess a wrong number'. It applies to ChatbotScreen.tsx:34/177, ContractionTimerScreen.tsx:37/107 and HealthDashboardScreen.tsx:210-215. An App Review tester in the US region who accepts the defaults sees 'call emergency (190)' on a red flag. The store copy (listing.json:43/56 'shows your country's emergency number') and the review notes (listing.json:74) make the same claim.
findings.fix_hint: (a) Default `country` to '' (no preselection) or to 'other' when the region is not in regionMap. Never default to 'tunisia'. (b) Add US/UK/CA (and any country present in EMERGENCY_NUMBERS) to regionMap and to both pickers. (c) In resolveEmergencyNumber, return null when country === 'other' (only use the locale fallback when country is empty/undefined for legacy profiles), and show the generic 'call your local emergency number' text. (d) Add a unit test: resolveEmergencyNumber('other','ar') === null, and onboarding default with regionCode 'US' !== 'tunisia'.

findings.evidence: The Firebase client config comes only from the gitignored app/.env (.gitignore:34 `.env`; firebase.ts:9-14 `apiKey: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY!` …). EAS uploads the project according to .gitignore (there is no .easignore), so .env never reaches the build worker. eas.json build.production.env holds only APP_ENV (eas.json:45-47), and nothing checks that the 6 EXPO_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_* variables are set. app.config.ts:99-112 guards the native plist/json but not these. The EAS env/secret migration is still listed as pending in ../CLAUDE.md ('EAS Secrets migration (6 secrets)'). RELEASE_READINESS §4 omits it and says that only a build command and store accounts remain. If the variables are not on EAS, initializeApp() runs with an undefined apiKey. Firebase Auth throws auth/invalid-api-key when the module is evaluated, and the binary crashes at launch — a certain 2.1 rejection. The local `expo export` passes only because .env is present on this machine ('env: load .env' in the export log).
findings.fix_hint: Owner: `eas env:create --environment production --name EXPO_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY …` ×6 (+ preview), visibility 'plaintext/sensitive'. Code (defence in depth): in app.config.ts, when APP_ENV is 'production' or 'preview', throw if any of the 6 EXPO_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_* variables is empty, like the existing plist guard. Add the item to RELEASE_READINESS §4.

findings.evidence: The public pages give a path that does not exist. delete-account.html:37-38 says 'Allez dans Réglages … Section Données & Vie Privée → Supprimer mon compte', and privacy.html:89 / privacy-en.html:84 / delete-account-en.html:37-38 say the same. SettingsScreen's 'Données & Vie Privée' section (366-452) contains only the PDF export and the JSON export. There is no delete row: the i18n key common.privacyData.deleteAccount exists in fr/common.json:439 but is never rendered. The only delete button is in ProfileScreen 'Zone de danger' (ProfileScreen.tsx:571-632). delete-account.html:70 also tells guests they 'can use Réglages → … → Supprimer mon compte', but the button is hidden for guests (`{!user?.isGuest && (` ProfileScreen.tsx:571). A reviewer who follows the published deletion instructions cannot find the feature, which is a 5.1.1(v) and Play deletion-policy risk.
findings.fix_hint: Either add a 'Supprimer mon compte' row to the Settings Data & Privacy section that runs the same confirm → deleteAccount → reauth flow as ProfileScreen (the key already exists), or rewrite the 4 website pages to say 'Accueil → avatar → Mon profil → Zone de danger → Supprimer mon compte'. Fix the guest sentence (guests: 'Réinitialiser le profil'). Then redeploy (F-001).

findings.evidence: The live privacy policy (fetched 2026-09-30) is an older version than the repo. It still says: 'Notifications Push (Expo / Firebase Cloud Messaging) : Un identifiant anonyme d'appareil ("push token") est envoyé aux serveurs d'Apple (APNs) ou de Google (FCM)' and 'Google Firebase Analytics : Données d'utilisation anonymes'. The app sends no push tokens (only local notifications; no getExpoPushTokenAsync/getDevicePushTokenAsync in src). It omits glucose, symptoms, the declared medical conditions (GDM, hypertension, twins), emergency contacts and assistant data, all of which the repo version lists. The URL entered in App Store Connect and Play is this live page, so the App Privacy label, the Data safety form and the policy will disagree (5.1.1(i), 5.1.2; Play User Data policy).
findings.fix_hint: Redeploy ../website (same deploy as F-001). Then diff live against repo for privacy.html and privacy-en.html.

findings.evidence: The in-app privacy policy, which Apple requires to be reachable in the app, is stale and incomplete. It says 'Dernière mise à jour : Décembre 2024' (fr/common.json:350; en/common.json:299) and has the footer '© 2024'. The collection section lists only email/first name, LMP/due date, weight and blood pressure, appointments and notification settings. It does not mention glucose, symptoms, kick counts or contractions, the optional declared medical conditions, emergency contacts or the Sentry crash reporting. It names no third party except Firebase, gives no retention period, and describes deletion as a request: 'deletionDesc': 'Demander la suppression de votre compte' (fr:389), although deletion is self-service. It contradicts the repo website policy (../website/privacy.html) that it is meant to mirror. Guideline 5.1.1(i) requires the policy to name all collected data, every third party that receives it, and retention and deletion practices.
findings.fix_hint: Regenerate the privacy.* keys in all 4 locales from ../website/privacy.html (sections 2-6): the full data list, Sentry as processor, the Firebase/Google Cloud location and transfer outside the EU, retention ('until you delete your account'), the in-app deletion path, and consent withdrawal for the medical flags. Update lastUpdated and the footer year. Or add a prominent 'Full policy' link that opens Constants.expoConfig.extra.privacyPolicyUrl, once F-005 is deployed.

findings.evidence: Most medical content has no source citations. The 80 articles have no sources/references field (keys: article_id…content_markdown_tn, none named source*), and none of the content_markdown_fr bodies has a 'Sources'/'Références' section (script check: 0/80). The weeks_db has no source field either (baby_dev_text_*, mom_body_text_*, warnings_text_*). ArticleDetailScreen renders no citation block. Only SupplementDetailScreen.tsx:298-299 shows `supplement.sources`. App Review routinely rejects health apps under 1.4.1 ('include citations to the medical information presented in the app'), and the listing's secondary category 'Medical' (listing.json:21) draws closer review.
findings.fix_hint: Add a `sources` field per article and per week (ACOG/HAS/NHS/WHO/CNGOF with URLs). Render a 'Sources' footer in ArticleDetailScreen and WeekRecommendations/Home week card, linked through safeOpenUrl. At minimum, add one app-wide 'Sources & méthodologie' screen that lists the references, and link it from Settings > Legal and from every article footer. Consider dropping the secondary 'Medical' category.

findings.evidence: The assistant is labelled beta in the app and in store metadata. ChatbotScreen.tsx:265 renders `<Text style={styles.botBetaBadgeText}>BETA</Text>` (hardcoded, not translated). The listing descriptions say '• Assistant multilingue (BÊTA)' and 'L'assistant est en version bêta', the whatsNew says 'Assistant multilingue (bêta)', and the review notes say 'the in-app assistant is explicitly labelled BETA'. Guideline 2.2 states that betas and trial versions do not belong on the App Store (use TestFlight), and 2.3 metadata rejections for 'beta' wording are common. Presenting the medical-triage assistant as unfinished also weakens the 1.4.1 position.
findings.fix_hint: Remove the BETA badge (ChatbotScreen.tsx:264-266) and the beta wording in all 3 listing locales and the review notes. Keep the permanent medical disclaimer (common.chatDisclaimer) and describe the assistant as an 'information assistant (not medical advice)'. Update __tests__/storeListing.test.ts if it asserts 'BETA'.

findings.evidence: 'See all' on the appointments card opens a placeholder instead of a feature: `onPress={() => showAlert(t('dashboard.soonAvailable'), t('dashboard.soonAvailableDesc'))}`, which shows 'Coming soon / Detailed tracking is coming soon!' (en/dashboard.json:26-27). This is a dead button with 'coming soon' copy on a primary health surface, and it is exactly what 2.1 (App Completeness) rejections cite.
findings.fix_hint: Navigate to the Calendar tab instead: `navigation.navigate('Calendrier', { screen: 'CalendarMain' })`, or remove the 'See all' link. Delete the dashboard.soonAvailable* keys once they are unused.

findings.evidence: On iOS, App Check is configured with `provider: __DEV__ ? 'debug' : 'appAttestWithDeviceCheckFallback'` (firebase.ts:72). App Attest needs the `com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment` entitlement, but app.json ios.entitlements contains only `"aps-environment": "production"` (app.json:20-22). The @react-native-firebase/app-check config plugin adds no entitlement (its plugin/build/ios contains only appDelegate.js). The DeviceCheck fallback covers only OS versions without App Attest, not a missing entitlement, so every iOS 14+ device fails attestation. APPCHECK_DEPLOYMENT.md tells the owner to register App Attest in the console, so enforcement would lock out iOS users.
findings.fix_hint: Add to app.json ios.entitlements: `"com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment": "production"`. EAS syncs the App Attest capability on the next credentials run. Document it in docs/APPCHECK_DEPLOYMENT.md.

findings.evidence: App Check is not active for any of the app's real traffic. Firestore and Auth use the Firebase JS SDK (`initializeFirestore(app, …)` firebase.ts:25, `createFirebaseAuth(app)` :20), but App Check is initialised only on the separate native @react-native-firebase app (firebase.ts:57-81). No `firebase/app-check` initializeAppCheck/CustomProvider bridges the native token into the JS app (grep: 0 hits). JS-SDK requests therefore carry no App Check token. Console metrics would show 100% unverified requests, and turning on enforcement (CLAUDE.md pending action #2, APPCHECK_DEPLOYMENT.md) would reject every Firestore and Auth call: a total outage for all users. The app.config.ts:20-26 comment ('A store binary with a dead anti-abuse layer is worse…') assumes this layer works, but it is inert.
findings.fix_hint: Bridge the tokens: `import { initializeAppCheck, CustomProvider } from 'firebase/app-check'; initializeAppCheck(app, { provider: new CustomProvider({ getToken: async () => { const { token } = await rnfbAppCheck().getToken(); return { token, expireTimeMillis: Date.now() + 55*60*1000 }; } }), isTokenAutoRefreshEnabled: true })`, as described in RNFB 'Using App Check with the JS SDK'. Warn the owner in APPCHECK_DEPLOYMENT.md: do NOT enforce until the verified-request ratio is at least 95%.

findings.evidence: `npm run import-data` (release doc §4 step 4) seeds Firestore `supplements` from repo-root supplements_pregnancy.json (importData.ts:38). That file is missing short_description_tn, pregnancy_notes_en/ar/tn, typical_dose_text_en/ar/tn and precautions_en/ar/tn; the bundled src/data/supplements_db.json has them. SupplementDetailScreen reads Firestore first and uses the bundle only if the doc is missing or the read errors (lines 72-86). Once the backend is live, EN/AR/TN users get dose and precaution text through the fallback chain in i18nHelpers.ts:26-29 (target → tn→ar → en → fr), which ends in French. Arabic and Tunisian users would read supplement dosages in French. The current web e2e cannot catch this because it runs with a dead backend and uses the bundle.
findings.fix_hint: Change importData.ts to seed from app/src/data/supplements_db.json (and articles from app/src/data/articles_db.json) instead of the stale repo-root copies. Or prefer the bundled record when the Firestore doc lacks the `_<lang>` field. Add a test that every seeded supplement has typical_dose_text_{fr,en,ar,tn}.

findings.evidence: docs/clinical-review/README.md:3-4 says '**aucun contenu médical de cette application n'a jamais été relu par un professionnel de santé.**' Only Ramadan and Halal are feature-flagged off (featureFlags.ts:29,48). The TRIAGE (chatbot red flags and HealthDashboard BP/glucose alerts), SUPPLEMENTS (doses such as 's02_fer … 100-200 mg par jour', 's03_vitamine_d … 100 000 UI'), FORBIDDEN_FOODS and MEDICAL_PROFILE dossiers, 55+3 claims in all, ship visible and unsigned. The listing claims 'The app flags the readings worth raising with your caregiver' (listing.json:56). This was known as owner gate GT-4 (RELEASE_READINESS §4 #5) and is still open. Rated P1 not P0 because the doses are hedged ('sur avis médical') and SupplementDetail shows common.supplementsDisclaimer.
findings.fix_hint: Owner: get the TRIAGE and SUPPLEMENTS dossiers signed by a midwife or OB before submission, as the README orders, and record the attestation in the commit. If the sign-off will not arrive before submission, add a SUPPLEMENT_DOSES_CLINICALLY_REVIEWED flag that hides typical_dose_text (SupplementDetailScreen.tsx:250-254) and shows 'ask your midwife for the dose' instead.

findings.evidence: The review notes still contain placeholders: '  email: <fill from GT-7>\n  password: <fill from GT-7>'. Calendar, cloud sync and health history are account-only, and guests cannot hold appointments (store/README.md). App Review rejects under 2.1 when account-gated features are listed without working demo credentials. Known as GT-7 and still open.
findings.fix_hint: Once the backend is activated, create the demo account with seeded data (appointments, weights, BP). Put the credentials only in App Store Connect > App Review Information and the Play Console 'App access' section, not in the git-tracked listing.json. Replace the placeholder with 'see App Review Information'.

findings.evidence: The notification permission is requested the first time Home renders, with no explanation. AppContent's effect runs `syncRemindersToNotifications(week, …)` as soon as `user && week > 0` (App.tsx:262-267), i.e. right after onboarding and on every cold launch. The sync loops over the 3 default_enabled reminders (rem_hyd_water, rem_med_prenatal_vitamins, rem_act_walk), and each call to scheduleReminderNotification calls requestNotificationPermissions() → Notifications.requestPermissionsAsync() (notificationService.ts:59,116). iOS and Android 13+ show the system dialog before the user has done anything, and a medication reminder is enabled without opt-in. RemindersTab's PermissionBanner also requests on mount (RemindersTab.tsx:69-75), not on tap. This goes against the HIG and the 4.5.4 spirit and lowers opt-in.
findings.fix_hint: In the sync path, check permission with getPermissionsAsync() and schedule only if it is already granted; never call requestPermissionsAsync from a background sync. Ask once, after a primer screen explaining the reminders (e.g. the first visit to the Reminders tab or at the end of onboarding), from a user tap. Make PermissionBanner call getPermissionsAsync on mount and request only in handlePress.

findings.evidence: Production Settings exposes a section marked '{/* Permissions Debug Section */}' (SettingsScreen.tsx:283), with a 'Test Notifications' button (:328-356). It is not gated by __DEV__, unlike the Developer Tools block at :476. Tapping it schedules 3 fake notifications in 3, 6 and 9 s (a fake appointment 'test rdv', a fake task and a hydration reminder; rdvNotificationService.ts:357-418), with alert text '3 test notifications sent! • Appointment (3 sec)…' (en/common.json:117). This is a debug tool in the release UI (2.1 / 4.0 polish). The Android test notifications also have no channelId.
findings.fix_hint: Wrap the 'Test Notifications' row in `__DEV__ &&`. Keep 'Request permissions' but rename the section comment, and move it into Reminders settings.

findings.evidence: The iOS project declares no localizations. There is no CFBundleLocalizations and no expo-localization `supportedLocales` option (app.json:185 lists the plugin as a bare 'expo-localization'). The local prebuild's Info.plist has CFBundleDevelopmentRegion only (ios/MamaBb/Info.plist). As a result, (a) the App Store product page 'Languages' row shows English only, although the app is fr/en/ar; (b) system-provided UI (Alert.prompt buttons used in the reauth flow ProfileScreen.tsx:596-611, share sheet, text-edit menus, the DateTimePicker chrome) appears in English for fr and ar users. The NSUserNotificationsUsageDescription (app.json:25) is French-only and is not a key iOS reads.
findings.fix_hint: Change the plugin entry to `["expo-localization", { "supportedLocales": { "ios": ["fr","en","ar"], "android": ["fr","en","ar"] } }]` (the plugin writes CFBundleLocalizations, see node_modules/expo-localization/plugin/build/withExpoLocalization.js:43-44). Drop the unused NSUserNotificationsUsageDescription or localize it through expo `locales`.

findings.evidence: The account purge can partly fail without anyone knowing. purgeUserFirestoreData wraps each collection in try/catch and only logs, `log.warn(\`Failed to cleanup collection ${colName}\`, err)` (gdprPurge.ts:70-72, :85-87). deleteAccount then deletes the Firebase Auth user regardless (AuthContext.tsx:708). If any query fails (missing index, a rules drift, offline mid-batch), those health documents are orphaned: their owner uid no longer exists, the user can no longer reach them, and the UI still navigates away as if deletion succeeded. The privacy policy promises 'Rien n'est conservé' (website/privacy.html:89-90). This is a GDPR Art. 17 / 5.1.1(v) integrity gap.
findings.fix_hint: Collect failures and throw before firebaseUser.delete() when any collection failed (e.g. `if (failures.length) throw new Error('PURGE_INCOMPLETE')`), and show a retry alert. Add a unit test: getDocs rejects for one collection → auth delete is NOT called.

findings.evidence: The review notes promise 'A permanent medical disclaimer is shown' (listing.json:74). In the app, medical disclaimers exist only on Chatbot (:270), Supplement detail (:309), Forbidden foods, Kick counter, Contraction timer and Health dashboard. Onboarding/AuthChoice shows only a data disclaimer: t('guestDisclaimer') = 'Your data won't be saved without an account'. ArticleDetail (80 medical articles) and the week pages (warnings_text_*) have none. The general 'not medical advice' text sits only inside the legal screen (legalTerms.terms.medical).
findings.fix_hint: Add a one-line common.medicalDisclaimer footer to ArticleDetailScreen and WeekRecommendationsScreen. Show a one-time medical-disclaimer acknowledgement at the end of onboarding (guest and account paths), and store its acceptance.

findings.evidence: `supportsTablet: true` (app.json:17) runs on iPad as a phone-width column centred on a blank canvas. The iPad 13" store screenshot (ipad-13/en/1-home.png) shows about 35% of the width used, with empty side margins and a full-width status bar over a narrow column. Guideline 2.4.1 and the 4.0 design reviews on iPad reject apps that 'do not take advantage of the iPad display' only occasionally, but it is a real risk. The owner accepted this at GT-6, so it is flagged as a risk, not a defect.
findings.fix_hint: Either set supportsTablet:false (the app then runs in iPhone compatibility mode, with no iPad screenshots or review on iPad), or widen TabletFrame's max width (about 700pt) and adapt the grid screens to 2 columns. Decide before the first iOS submission, because changing supportsTablet after release is irreversible (you cannot drop iPad support later).

findings.evidence: Several mandatory console forms are not on the owner's to-do list. RELEASE_READINESS §4 omits Play 'Health apps declaration' (mandatory for Health & Fitness/Medical), the Data safety form (with Sentry as a third-party recipient and the working deletion URL, F-001), Apple App Privacy answers and Play 'App access'. They are recorded only in the older plan (GOAL_STORE_RELEASE:256-262). Play cannot publish with App content items incomplete. These forms must also match the corrected privacy policy (F-005/F-006) and the privacy manifest (F-023).
findings.fix_hint: Add these to RELEASE_READINESS §4 as explicit owner steps in this order: deploy website → App Privacy (Apple) → Data safety + Health apps declaration + App access + Ads = No + Target audience 18+ (Play).

findings.evidence: Some Tunisian strings are in Latin-script Arabizi/French while the rest of the tn locale is in Arabic script and renders RTL: 'legal': 'Support w 9anoun' (:124), 'dangerZone': 'Zonèt danger' (:125, the Danger-zone header over the Delete-account button), 'preferences': 'Réglagat' (:127). Mixed LTR Latin runs in the RTL UI look like untranslated leftovers. The ar equivalents are Arabic.
findings.fix_hint: Replace them with Arabic-script Tunisian (e.g. 'الدعم والقانون', 'منطقة الخطر', 'الإعدادات'), matching the ar entries. Add an i18n test: tn values containing [A-Za-z]{3,} and no Arabic letters must be allowlisted (units like mmHg, 'Firebase', the email placeholder).

findings.evidence: The privacy manifest does not match what the app collects. It declares NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeProductInteraction for purpose Analytics (app.json:101-108), but analytics is a no-op on native: firebase.ts:97-101 says `isSupported()` resolves false and 'All analyticsService methods are intentionally no-ops'. Meanwhile Sentry runs with `tracesSampleRate: 0.2` (App.tsx:23), i.e. performance data, which is not declared (NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePerformanceData). CrashData is declared Linked=false, but logger.setUser attaches a stable SHA-256(uid) to every Sentry event (logger.ts:176-185), and Apple counts a stable identifier as linked. The App Privacy label will be inaccurate in both directions.
findings.fix_hint: Remove ProductInteraction/Analytics, or keep it only if you keep Sentry breadcrumbs/touch tracking. Add PerformanceData (AppFunctionality). Set CrashData Linked=true, or stop calling Sentry.setUser. Keep the App Store Connect App Privacy answers identical.

findings.evidence: Android channels are created only inside requestNotificationPermissions (notificationService.ts:70-85), and the 'default' channel name is hardcoded English: `name: 'General'` (:82). It appears untranslated in Android system settings for fr, ar and tn users. Hydration reminders (hydrationService.ts:120) and one-time task notifications (notificationService.ts:179) are scheduled without a channelId, so they land on the unlocalized 'default'/fallback channel with DEFAULT importance, unlike the 'pregnancy-reminders' HIGH channel.
findings.fix_hint: Create both channels once at startup (native only) with i18n names (notifications.channelName / channelNameGeneral in 4 locales), and pass channelId: 'pregnancy-reminders' in the hydration and one-time triggers.

findings.evidence: The linking prefixes are `['mama-bebe://', 'exp+mama-bebe://', 'https://mama-bebe.com']`, but app.json declares no `scheme`. The generated native projects register only 'com.mamabebe.app' (iOS) and 'exp+mama-bebe' (dev client), so mama-bebe:// links do nothing in store builds. 'https://mama-bebe.com' is not the product domain (mama-et-bebe.com), and no associatedDomains or intent-filter autoVerify exists, so that prefix is dead too. Harmless today, but misleading.
findings.fix_hint: Add `"scheme": "mama-bebe"` to app.json, or drop the prefix. Replace the https prefix with https://www.mama-et-bebe.com only if universal links are set up (ios.associatedDomains + apple-app-site-association); otherwise remove it.

findings.evidence: `"appleTarget": "12+"` and the note 'Answer Apple's questionnaire with Infrequent/Mild Medical…': Apple's 2025 age-rating system (4+/9+/13+/16+/18+, new questionnaire with medical/wellness and user-generated-content questions) no longer has a 12+ tier. The guidance is outdated for the questionnaire the owner will actually see.
findings.fix_hint: Update the note: answer the new questionnaire honestly (medical/treatment information: yes; unrestricted web access: no), which is expected to yield 13+. Keep Play IARC as planned.

findings.evidence: For a first public release, promotionalText announces an upgrade: fr 'Nouvelle version : rappels plus fins, contenus enrichis…', en 'New: finer-grained reminders, a richer content library…', ar 'جديد: …'. This misleads when there is no previous version. The keywords also spend characters on a word already indexed from the app name ('bebe' in fr, 'baby' in en; Apple indexes the name).
findings.fix_hint: Rewrite promotionalText as a value statement (e.g. 'Votre grossesse semaine par semaine, en 4 langues, avec rappels et suivi santé.'). Replace 'bebe' and 'baby' in keywords with unused terms (e.g. 'echographie' / 'ultrasound', 'contraction').

findings.evidence: The Arabic brand name differs between app and store. In the app, ar/common.json:474 `"appName": "ماما وطفلي"`, which is also used in the privacy text (:310) and the footers (:358, :638), 8 occurrences across ar and tn. The Arabic store listing name is 'ماما وبيبي — الحمل' (listing.json:64). Users see two different names.
findings.fix_hint: Pick one Arabic brand (the listing uses وبيبي) and apply it to all 8 i18n occurrences, or change the listing to match.

findings.evidence: The live Firebase Web API key (identical to the one in app/.env) is committed in two tracked docs: `X-Goog-Api-Key: AIzaSyBC7HcO…`. Firebase web keys are public by design (the key is also inlined in the JS bundle), so the protection is the GCP key restriction and App Check. The restriction is still pending (CLAUDE.md pending #4), and App Check is inert (F-011).
findings.fix_hint: Owner: restrict the key in GCP (iOS bundle id + Android package/SHA-1, API allowlist: Identity Toolkit, Firestore, Token Service, Firebase App Check). Optionally redact the key from the 2 docs.

findings.evidence: 'Dernière mise à jour : 16 Février 2026', but the policy content was substantially rewritten in commit 9cae9fe (after the release-readiness date 2026-08-19). The stated date predates the changes it describes.
findings.fix_hint: Set the date to the deploy date of the new text, in privacy.html and privacy-en.html.

findings.evidence: After a successful delete, `navigation.reset({ index: 0, routes: [{ name: 'AuthChoice' }] })` is sent from inside HomeStack, and 'AuthChoice' is registered only in AuthStack. The RESET is unhandled (a dev-mode error; silently ignored in prod), and the user lands on the Language screen once `user` becomes null, not on AuthChoice. Separately, in the REAUTH_REQUIRED path the Firestore data is already purged (AuthContext.tsx:699) before auth.delete fails. If the user cancels the password prompt, they stay signed in with an empty account and no explanation.
findings.fix_hint: Drop the navigation.reset calls (setUser(null) already swaps to AuthStack). Or reauthenticate before purging: call reauthenticateWithCredential first when auth_time is older than 5 minutes, so the purge and the auth delete happen together. On cancel, show 'your data was deleted; confirm your password to finish deleting the account'.
